title: Raise the minimum supported Python version to 3.11
outOfScope: The stevedore 5.9.0 dependency update itself; it remains in the deferred #444 Work Item until this migration is merged.
Any unrelated dependency, workflow-action, release tag, release asset, or Dependabot PR update.
Changes to historical archived Work Item evidence.

sources.reason: Human authorization to raise the minimum supported Python version to 3.11 before resuming #444.
The blocked stevedore 5.9.0 update requires Python >=3.11.
Current direct development dependency input pin whose successor cannot resolve under Python 3.10.
Current hash-pinned development dependency closure and release evidence input.
Current hosted Python compatibility matrix and Python 3.10 lockfile compiler baseline.
English public runtime prerequisite; Chinese and Japanese equivalents require semantic alignment.
Authoritative pre-release execution order and bidirectional traceability plan.

rawUserRequest: 最低版本升至 Python 3.11：先执行独立兼容性迁移，再合并 #444。

declaredIntent.summary: Raise AI Cockpit's minimum supported Python baseline from 3.10 to 3.11 across runtime validation, static tooling, hosted compatibility, reproducible dependency evidence, public documentation, and release claims before accepting the separately governed stevedore 5.9.0 update.

riskAssessment.reason: Changing a published runtime minimum intentionally removes Python 3.10 support and affects installers, CI, static tooling, lockfile reproduction, release evidence, and three public languages.

executionDecision.reason: The user explicitly authorized the minimum-version migration as the prerequisite to #444; the migration has a dedicated branch and must close before #444 is resumed.

preReviewWarnings: Do not merge #444 in this Work Item; prove Python 3.11 support and remove only the Python 3.10 baseline claims before resuming its separate branch.
Historical archive records must remain immutable even where they mention Python 3.10.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Record checkpoints before implementation and archival to prevent scope drift across the public compatibility migration.

acceptance: Every current runtime and static-tooling minimum changes from Python 3.10 to Python 3.11: ai_doctor, pyproject ruff/mypy targets, and lockfile compiler normalization.
The blocking hosted Python matrix and lockfile-reproducibility job no longer test or compile with 3.10, retain 3.11 and 3.14 coverage, and focused regression tests reject a 3.10 baseline.
The direct dependency input and deterministic lockfile are regenerated on Python 3.11 with stevedore remaining at 5.8.0; no 5.9.0 #444 change appears in this migration diff.
English, Chinese, and Japanese README, quick-start, and installation guidance consistently require Python 3.11+, while distribution documentation accurately describes the release-blocking baseline.

Source-bound supply-chain, capability-truth, Japanese-assessment, serial-plan, and traceability evidence reflect the completed migration; the supply-chain refresh synchronizes a changed lockfile digest into release.json instead of leaving stale release evidence; all 16 local governance gates, full quality, and fresh hosted CI pass before merge.
guidelines: Treat the Python 3.11 minimum as a public compatibility contract, not a local tooling preference.
Regenerate lockfile and source-bound evidence with their declared commands; do not hand-edit generated data.
Preserve historical archive evidence and keep #444's stevedore change on its own Work Item branch.
Keep English, Chinese, and Japanese prerequisites semantically aligned.

intent.problem: stevedore 5.9.0 requires Python >=3.11, while AI Cockpit publicly and operationally supports Python 3.10+. The mismatch blocks a requested pre-release dependency intake and leaves conflicting compatibility evidence.
constraints: Raise the minimum only to Python 3.11, not a newer version.
Use a dedicated migration PR before any #444 dependency change.
Do not edit archive history or merge/update #444 in this Work Item.
Prove the new baseline locally and with fresh hosted CI before merge.
intent.rationale: An explicit, comprehensive migration makes the intentional support change reviewable and evidence-bound, then allows #444 to be resumed without weakening the compatibility or lockfile gates.

problemStatement: Migrate the published and enforced Python compatibility baseline to 3.11+ so the repository can later accept stevedore 5.9.0 without falsely claiming Python 3.10 support.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: Python 3.10 is rejected while Python 3.11 is accepted by runtime diagnostics and documented prerequisite validation
scenarioCoverage.expected: ai_doctor and documentation metadata use Python 3.11 as the sole current minimum, with no active public 3.10 prerequisite marker.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Add focused doctor and docs metadata regression tests, then run their complete modules.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: Hosted blocking compatibility and lockfile reproduction use the new baseline
scenarioCoverage.expected: compatibility.yml matrix includes 3.11 and 3.14 but not 3.10; its lockfile compiler is 3.11 and Makefile normalization is canonical 3.11.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Add focused workflow/orchestration tests and run lockfile reproducibility under Python 3.11, then inspect hosted CI.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: Migration does not absorb the deferred stevedore update
scenarioCoverage.expected: The migrated input and lockfile retain stevedore 5.8.0; #444 remains unmerged and is resumed only after this Work Item closes.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Run focused pin assertions, diff ownership, check-ai-pr, and inspect the final PR diff.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: All three public languages and release evidence make the same compatibility claim
scenarioCoverage.expected: English, Chinese, Japanese and distribution documentation say Python 3.11+; generated capability and supply-chain records match the final source state.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Run documentation, multilingual, supply-chain, capability-truth, Japanese assessment, full quality, and hosted CI checks.

restrictedWriteApproval.reason: The user explicitly approved the Python 3.11 compatibility migration and the related CI, runtime, documentation, generated-evidence, and governance updates.

rollbackNote: Revert this migration PR to restore the Python 3.10 compatibility contract and its prior lockfile, workflow, tooling, documentation, and generated evidence; do not merge #444 until a replacement compatibility decision is made.
